newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LEICESTERSHIRE SNATCH LEAD IN THRILLING TITLE RACE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LEICESTERSHIRE SNATCH LEAD IN THRILLING TITLE RACE.

text.p: Leicestershire edged ahead in the compelling race for the English county championship when they survived some anxious moments to beat Nottinghamshire by six wickets on Friday.
Captain James Whitaker calmed Leicestershire nerves with an unbeaten 30 to steer his side to the victory target of 82 after their first three wickets tumbled for 40.
Leicestershire's win on the fourth and final day at Trent Bridge gave them a one-point lead in the most open championship for many years.
The top five teams -- Leicestershire, Surrey, Derbyshire, Essex and Kent -- all have realistic title ambitions and are separated by only 15 points with two matches left.

Leicestershire, seeking only the second championship in their 117-year history, swiftly polished off Nottinghamshire's second innings in the morning, pace bowler David Millns taking the remaining two wickets.

Millns finished with five for 31 as Notts were dismissed for 196, but the home team hit back through a three-wicket burst with the new ball by Mark Bowen before Whitaker came in to seal success at 82 for four.
Surrey moved into second place after completing an emphatic 225-run victory over Northamptonshire at The Oval.
Northants were 173 for six overnight in pursuit of a target of 459 to win and resisted for 100 minutes, losing David Ripley retired injured along the way.
Australian Brendon Julian, who had a match haul of eight for 80, and fellow paceman Joey Benjamin shared the three wickets to fall as Northants were all out for 233.
Third-placed Derbyshire's attempt to go top of the table was frustrated by Somerset in a drawn match at Taunton.
Derbyshire's Australian captain Dean Jones, perhaps wary of losing in a high-scoring game, declared his second innings at 322 for six, leaving 78 overs to bowl Somerset out for less than 383.
Opener Mark Lathwell (54) and Peter Bowler (60) attacked the target at an average of five runs an over, until their second wicket stand of 79 was broken and Somerset appeared to lose their nerve.

England paceman Dominic Cork captured three wickets in 28 balls as Somerset slipped to 141 for five but Derbyshire were then thwarted by Rob Turner (49) and pace bowler Jason Kerr, who hit a championship best of 68 not out. They steered their side to 296 for eight at the finish.
Essex are fourth after beating Warwickshire by 170 runs at Edgbaston for the sixth win in their last seven championship games.
Paceman Neil Williams (4-57) and off-spinner Peter Such (4-114) were the Essex attacking spearheads as Warwickshire were bowled out for 265 in the face of an improbable victory target of 436.
Leicestershire lead the title chasers with 248 points from Surrey (247), Derbyshire (242), Essex (241) and Kent (233), who were not involved in the current round of matches.
